items.text: A closed Linux window can be undone from any other window.
Linux keeps stashed panes hidden across a relaunch, and resize, equalize, swap and drops skip them.
On Linux, remote windows, tabs and splits use the machine's Host Settings shell and folder, as on the Mac.
A split or new tab of a WSL pane starts in that pane's folder when WSL is the default shell.
The rail reuses each resting tile's glassy rim instead of redrawing it pixel by pixel on every paint.
A pane sidebar scroll step is measured on Windows in Mac's 40-window scene, and costs about 4 ms.
